text: {"overall_winner":"B","qualities":[{"evidence":"introduces a future-tech debate and poses questions about blame and roadways","quality":"engaging introduction","description":"The essay opens by framing the topic in a broader context and drawing the reader into the argument with pointed questions."},{"evidence":"states both benefits and risks before taking a side","quality":"balanced argumentation","description":"The essay acknowledges counterpoints while still building a case, which makes the argument feel more credible and considered."},{"evidence":"several paragraphs organized around positives, risks, law, and conclusion","quality":"organization","description":"The essay follows a clearer structure that separates major claims into distinct sections and keeps the line of reasoning easier to follow."},{"evidence":"focuses on fuel efficiency, emissions, money saved, and legal liability","quality":"development of reasoning","description":"The essay develops its position with multiple linked claims instead of repeating the same idea in slightly different words."},{"evidence":"return of zero accidents, multiple safety precautions, real driver in them at all times","quality":"use of evidence","description":"The essay grounds its claims more consistently in details from the source article rather than relying mostly on general statements."},{"evidence":"restates the argument as facts on the side of driverless cars","quality":"conclusion","description":"The ending clearly synthesizes the main points and brings the essay back to its overall claim."}]}
